claim_1.claim: Hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons at day 28 after vaccination (day 28) showed that antibody responses decreased with age compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age (Figures 1B, 1C, and S1C), consistent with previous studies (Seidman et al., 2012). Vaccines from different seasons induced varying levels of HAI responses, and there was a significant decrease in the response with age (Figure 1C).

Figure 1. Experimental Approach and Humoral Immunity to Influenza Vaccination in Young and Elderly (B) HAI responses by season. The maximum HAI response (highest day 28-day 0 fold-induction among all three strains) is shown for all 212 subjects separated by flu season, along with box plots indicating the first and third quartiles and median. For 2010 and 2011, subjects are also separated into young (<65 years old) and elderly (65 or older). p values represent results of independent two-sample t test between responses of young and elderly. (C) Correlation of HAI responses with age in the 2010 season and 2011 season. R and p represent the Pearson correlation coefficient and associated p value, respectively.

claim_2.claim: Hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 influenza seasons at day 28 after vaccination (day 28) showed no significant difference in antibody response based on gender, diabetic status, or race compared to the corresponding reference groups.

sources.quote: There was no significant difference in antibody response based on gender (Figure S1D), diabetic status (Figure S1E), or race (data not shown). There was no significant difference in the response between males and females in any of the seasons examined (data not shown).

claim_3.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that blood transcription modules related to induction of interferons and activation of dendritic cells on days 1 and 3 after vaccination (days 1 and 3) were positively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 28 antibody response, whereas T-cell-related modules at these time points were negatively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 28 antibody response.

sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells (Figures 2A and 2B) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.

Figure 2. Signatures Associated with the Antibody Response Induced by TIV (A) Heat map of blood transcription modules (BTMs, rows) and TIV seasons (columns) whose activity at days 1, 3, or 7 after vaccination is associated with HAI response at day 28 after vaccination. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA, nominal p < 0.05; 1,000 permutations) was used to identify positive (red), negative (blue), or no (gray) enrichment of BTMs (gene sets) within pre-ranked gene lists, where genes were ranked according to their correlation between expression and HAI response.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that antibody-secreting-cell and cell-cycle-related modules on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) were positively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 28 antibody response.

sources.quote: On day 7, there was a robust enrichment of ASC and cell cycle-related modules, consistent with our original study (Nakaya et al., 2011).

Figure 2. Signatures Associated with the Antibody Response Induced by TIV (A) Heat map of blood transcription modules (BTMs, rows) and TIV seasons (columns) whose activity at days 1, 3, or 7 after vaccination is associated with HAI response at day 28 after vaccination. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA, nominal p < 0.05; 1,000 permutations) was used to identify positive (red), negative (blue), or no (gray) enrichment of BTMs (gene sets) within pre-ranked gene lists, where genes were ranked according to their correlation between expression and HAI response.

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from subjects across multiple influenza vaccine seasons, using discriminant analysis via mixed integer programming (DAMIP), showed that sets of discriminatory genes predicted the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) response in the blind testing group with 67.6%–70.0% accuracy.

sources.quote: Here DAMIP was able to correctly predict the HAI response in the blind testing group with 67.6%–70.0% accuracy (Tables S1 and S2).

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly TIV vaccinees across multiple influenza seasons, using single-sample GSEA and an artificial neural network classifier, showed that blood transcription modules on days 3 and 7 after vaccination (days 3 and 7) predicted hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) responses in both young and elderly groups compared to non-predictive classification.

sources.quote: With this approach, we identified BTMs that predicted HAI responses in both the young and elderly groups with accuracies ranging between 79.0% and 80.2% and between 64.7% and 72.3%, respectively, using both day 3 and day 7 signatures (Figure 2C).

Figure 2. Signatures Associated with the Antibody Response Induced by TIV (C and D) Identification of BTMs that predict antibody responses via neural network analysis. Single sample GSEA (Barbie et al., 2009) enrichment scores were generated for each BTM on day 3 and day 7 after vaccination in 85% of the young subjects (training set) and used as inputs to an artificial neural network classifier to predict the day 28 antibody responses, in the remaining 15% of the young (young test set) or the elderly (elderly test set) subjects.

claim_7.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across five influenza seasons and independent validation datasets, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that pre-vaccination B-cell- and T-cell-related modules were positively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 28 antibody response, whereas pre-vaccination monocyte-related modules were negatively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 28 antibody response.

sources.quote: This approach revealed several B-cell- and T-cell-related modules whose expression pre-vaccination was positively correlated with an increased antibody response to vaccination in all studies (Figure 3A). In contrast, modules related to monocytes were negatively correlated with antibody responses (Figures 3B–3G).

Figure 3. Baseline Signatures Are Associated with the Antibody Response (A) Heat map of BTMs (rows) and TIV studies (columns) whose activity before vaccination is associated with HAI response at day 28 after vaccination. GSEA (nominal p < 0.05; 1,000 permutations) was used to identify positive (red) or negative (blue) enrichment of BTMs (gene sets) within pre-ranked gene lists, where genes were ranked according to their correlation between expression and HAI response.

claim_8.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from young (<65 years) and elderly (≥65 years) vaccinees in the 2010 season at days 1, 3, 7, and 14 after vaccination, using differential expression analysis, showed that the young exhibited a greater number of both up- and downregulated genes on day 1 after vaccination (day 1) compared to the elderly.

sources.quote: By far the largest difference in overall expression between the two groups occurred on day 1, where the young exhibited a much greater number of both up- and downregulated genes.

Figure 4. Molecular Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young Adults and in Elderly (A) Number of genes differentially expressed (log2 fold-change > 0.2 and t test p value < 0.01) in young (<65 years) (left) and elderly (≥65 years) (right) vaccinees on days 1, 3, 7, and 14 after vaccination (2010 season).

claim_9.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 season, using weighted correlation network analysis, showed that interferon-related genes shared by young and elderly clusters had higher expression in young individuals compared to elderly individuals.

sources.quote: Although the genes shared by clusters from young and elderly vaccinated individuals had similar temporal expression profiles, the magnitude of the expression of interferon-related genes differed, being higher in young individuals (Figure 4C).

Figure 4. Molecular Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young Adults and in Elderly (C) Temporal expression patterns of 197 interferon-related genes in common between modules Y1 and E1 from (B). Black line represents the mean fold change of all genes.

claim_10.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that NK-cell-related modules on days 3 and 7 after vaccination (days 3 and 7) and monocyte modules on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) increased with age, whereas many B-cell modules on days 3 and 7 after vaccination (days 3 and 7) decreased with age compared to younger subjects.

sources.quote: Natural killer (NK) cell-related modules showed increased expression with age on both day 3 and day 7 after vaccination, and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age on day 7. In contrast, many B cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects on both day 3 and day 7.

Figure 4. Molecular Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young Adults and in Elderly (D) BTMs (rows) whose activity at days 3 or 7 after vaccination (columns) is associated with the age of vaccinees from 2010 and 2011 seasons. GSEA (nominal p < 0.05; 1,000 permutations) was used to identify positive (red) or negative (blue) enrichment of BTMs (gene sets) within pre-ranked gene lists, where genes were ranked according to their correlation between expression and increasing age.

claim_11.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees in the 2010 and 2011 seasons at day 7 after vaccination (day 7), using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that B-cell modules M47.0 and M69 were positively associated with younger age and with high hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody responses, whereas monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules S4, M4.3, and M11.0 were positively associated with older age and negatively associated with hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody responses.

sources.quote: Two B cell modules, M47.0 and M69, showed increased expression in younger subjects and in subjects with high antibody responses, whereas three monocyte- and myeloid-cell-related modules, S4, M4.3, and M11.0, were enriched in the elderly and were also associated with a decreased antibody response in the 2010 and 2011 seasons.

Figure 4. Molecular Signatures Induced by Vaccination with TIV in Young Adults and in Elderly (F) BTMs whose activity at day 7 after vaccination is correlated with the age of vaccinees (x axis) and/or is correlated with HAI response (y axis) in both 2010 and 2011 seasons.

claim_12.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort at days 0–14 after vaccination showed that total NK-cell proportions were higher in elderly subjects than in young subjects at baseline (day 0) and at all studied time points.

sources.quote: Our analysis showed that proportions of total NK cells in elderly subjects were higher than those of young subjects at baseline as well as at all the time points studied (days 0–14).

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (A) Changes in total NK cell population after vaccination represented as percent within all PBMCs for young and elderly. Mean ± SEM. Areas under curve (AUC) in (A) and (C) were calculated to compare magnitudes of total NK cells and NK cells subsets between young and elderly cohorts throughout the study duration (days 0–14) and compared by t test.

claim_13.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from elderly subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at days 0–14 after vaccination showed that vaccination increased the percentage of total NK cells compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination (Figure 5A).

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (A) Changes in total NK cell population after vaccination represented as percent within all PBMCs for young and elderly. Mean ± SEM. Changes of each of the NK subset on the indicated time points after vaccination were compared to the day 0 (baseline) time point by t test.

claim_14.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at day 1 after vaccination (day 1) showed that vaccination reduced the percentage of total NK cells compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination (Figure 5A).

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (A) Changes in total NK cell population after vaccination represented as percent within all PBMCs for young and elderly. Mean ± SEM. Changes of each of the NK subset on the indicated time points after vaccination were compared to the day 0 (baseline) time point by t test.

claim_15.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at baseline (day 0) showed that elderly subjects had a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells compared to young subjects.

sources.quote: We observed a higher frequency of CD56dimCD16++ cells coincident with a lower frequency of CD56++ cells in the elderly at baseline, consistent with previous studies (Figure 5C; Solana et al., 2014).

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (C) Kinetics of magnitudes of CD56++ NK, CD56++CD16+ NK, and CD56dimCD16++ NK cell subsets in young (left) and elderly (right) after vaccination. Mean ± SEM.

claim_16.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from elderly subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at day 1 after vaccination (day 1) showed that CD56dimCD16++ NK cells increased compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56dimCD16++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (C) Kinetics of magnitudes of CD56++ NK, CD56++CD16+ NK, and CD56dimCD16++ NK cell subsets in young (left) and elderly (right) after vaccination. Mean ± SEM. Changes of each of the NK subset on the indicated time points after vaccination were compared to the day 0 (baseline) time point by t test.

claim_17.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at day 7 after vaccination (day 7) showed that CD56++ NK cells increased compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56dimCD16++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (C) Kinetics of magnitudes of CD56++ NK, CD56++CD16+ NK, and CD56dimCD16++ NK cell subsets in young (left) and elderly (right) after vaccination. Mean ± SEM. Changes of each of the NK subset on the indicated time points after vaccination were compared to the day 0 (baseline) time point by t test.

claim_18.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort at days 0, 1, 3, 7, and 14 after vaccination showed that CD69 expression on all three NK-cell subsets increased after vaccination in elderly subjects, with highest expression on day 3 (day 3), compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increasing activation after vaccination in all three subsets, with highest expression on day 3.

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (D) Activation of each of the NK cell subsets were assessed by CD69 staining and compared with day 0 (baseline) by t test. Data are represented as the geometric mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) for young (left) and elderly (right) at each time point, mean ± SEM.

claim_19.claim: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly subjects in a subset of the 2010 cohort showed that CD69 expression on the CD56dimCD16++ NK-cell subset increased only on day 1 after vaccination (day 1) in young subjects and was lower than in elderly subjects compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: In contrast, the young exhibited activation of the CD56dimCD16++ subset as measured by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.

Figure 5. Flow Cytometry Analysis of NK Cells in Young and Elderly after TIV Vaccination (D) Activation of each of the NK cell subsets were assessed by CD69 staining and compared with day 0 (baseline) by t test. Data are represented as the geometric mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) for young (left) and elderly (right) at each time point, mean ± SEM.

claim_20.claim: Hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from a subset of vaccinees measured through day 180 after vaccination showed that antibody responses peaked at day 28 after vaccination (day 28), measured at days 0, 28, and 180, compared to the other sampled time points.

sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 (Figure 6A).

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (A) HAI response (fold change of HAI titer relative to baseline) through 180 days for temporary (n = 28) and persistent (n = 34) responders.

claim_21.claim: Hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from a subset of vaccinees measured through day 180 after vaccination showed that antibody responses declined by day 180 after vaccination (day 180) compared to day 28 after vaccination (day 28).

sources.quote: The antibody responses peaked at day 28 (D28), with a significant decline in most subjects by D180 (Figure 6A).

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (A) HAI response (fold change of HAI titer relative to baseline) through 180 days for temporary (n = 28) and persistent (n = 34) responders.

claim_22.claim: Hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assay analysis of plasma from 62 vaccinees at days 28 and 180 after vaccination showed that the day 180 antibody response was positively associated with the day 28 hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody response.

sources.quote: Because the D180 antibody titer shows significant dependence on the original antibody response generated on day 28 (Figure 6B), examining the molecular profile associated with the D180 response would identify many of the mechanisms responsible for generating the D28 response.

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (B) Comparison between day 28 and day 180 HAI responses. Each symbol represents a single vaccinee and the color represents the season that they were vaccinated (n = 62). Black lines represent the regression line (Pearson) for all vaccinees combined.

claim_23.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 62 vaccinees at day 7 after vaccination (day 7), using blood transcription module analysis, showed that plasmablast module S3 activity was positively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 180 antibody response.

sources.quote: As expected, correlation analysis of plasmablast module BTM S3 shows a positive association with the D180 antibody response due to the effect of D28 antibody responses, generated through plasmablast expansion (Figure 6C).

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (C) Comparison between “S3 Plasma” BTM activity and the HAI responses at day 28 after vaccination. Each symbol represents a single vaccinee and the color represents the season that they were vaccinated (n = 62).

claim_24.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 62 vaccinees at day 7 after vaccination (day 7), using blood transcription module analysis, showed that plasmablast module S3 activity was not associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 180/day 28 antibody titer residual.

sources.quote: However, when we performed correlation between the plasmablast module activity and the D180/D28 residual, we no longer saw an association with the plasmablast expression (Figure 6D).

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (D) Comparison between “S3 Plasma” BTM activity and the HAI D180/D28 residual. Each symbol represents a single vaccinee and the color represents the season that they were vaccinated (n = 62).

claim_25.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees from the 2007 to 2010 seasons at days 3 and 7 after vaccination (days 3 and 7), using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that cell movement- and adhesion-related modules, including BTM M51, were positively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 180/day 28 antibody titer residual.

sources.quote: Among the BTMs most enriched in subjects with a persistent response on both days 3 and 7 were several modules associated with cell movement and adhesion, such as BTM 51 (Figure 6E).

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (E) Genes in BTM M51.0; each “edge” (gray line) represents a coexpression relationship, as described in Li et al. (2014); colors represent the correlation between baseline-normalized gene expression at day 3 after vaccination and the D180/D28 residual.

claim_26.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from vaccinees from the 2007 to 2010 seasons, using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), showed that day 7 expression of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 180/day 28 antibody titer residual.

sources.quote: In addition, the day 7 expression of a number of T-cell-related modules was negatively associated with the D180/D28 residual, indicating that increased T cell responses might potentially result in more transient antibody responses (Figure 6F).

Figure 6. Signatures Associated with the Persistence of TIV-Induced Antibody Response (F) BTMs (bars) whose activity at day 7 after vaccination is significantly associated with the HAI D180/D28 residual (GSEA; nominal p < 0.05; 1,000 permutations). Vaccinees from 2007 to 2010 seasons were combined. BTMs related to T cell functions (pink bars) or monocyte functions (purple bars) are shown.

claim_27.claim: MicroRNA expression profiling analysis of samples from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort at days 1, 3, and 7 after vaccination showed that miRNA profiles differed between young and elderly vaccinees, with most differentially expressed miRNAs upregulated in the elderly, particularly on days 1 and 7, compared to young vaccinees, who showed predominantly downregulated miRNAs.

sources.quote: We saw a significant difference in the miRNA profiles between these two groups. Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.

Figure 7. MicroRNA Expression Profiling of Young and Elderly TIV Vaccinees (A) Heat map of miRNAs (rows) up- (red) or downregulated (blue) at days 1, 3, and 7 after vaccination in young and elderly (columns); paired t test (p < 0.05); total number of differentially expressed miRNAs are shown at the bottom.

claim_28.claim: MicroRNA expression profiling analysis of samples from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort at days 1, 3, and 7 after vaccination showed that elderly vaccinees had a larger number of miRNAs negatively associated with the hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) day 28 antibody response compared to young vaccinees.

sources.quote: We again saw differences between the young and elderly subjects, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNA negatively correlating with the antibody response when compared with the young.

Figure 7. MicroRNA Expression Profiling of Young and Elderly TIV Vaccinees (B) MicroRNAs whose expression is positively or negatively correlated with HAI response in young and elderly; Pearson correlation (p < 0.05).
